messages:
sam: Heads-up: we've been seeing probes and hedged requests spike after the policy hot-reload last night. Looks like async decision snapshotting is causing slightly inconsistent routing slabs between replicas. Hedging up ~2.4% and tail latency nudging 30ms on p90. Anyone saw this in sim?
anya: saw a small bump in staging. hypothesis: snapshot epoch isn't being propagated to the decision cache fast enough, so probes get evaluated against old weights -> decisions disagree -> hedges.
kevin_r: +1. root cause sounds like 'decision epoch' divergence. currently we do: write snapshot -> async propagate -> replicas apply when they pull. There's a window where requests hit mixed epochs.
maria: can you paste the staging logs? curious which signals mismatch (latency vs cost vs region).
sam: logs: ``router:received_decision_epoch=202603, router:applied_epoch=202602`` repeated, then ``route:hedged_request=true reason=epoch_mismatch`` 
anya: short-term mitigation: attach epoch to request and have runtime prefer same-epoch routes. We already add metadata for explainability; extend it to force-consistency w/in request lifetime.
kevin_r: two concerns: 1) forcing same-epoch could reduce available capacity (if most replicas are new epoch), 2) adds coupling that may increase latencies while waiting for matching epoch. We should measure tradeoff.
tj: what about an async reconciliation token instead: add X-Decision-Epoch header and a policy that says fallback_when_mismatch=allow|strict with TTL. Default allow, canary strict for a subset of tenants.
maria: agree on canary. Also add metrics: routing.decision.epoch_mismatch_count, routing.decision.epoch_wait_time_ms, routing.hedge_rate_by_epoch. Need to wire into Console.
anya: proposal sketch:
```
# decision snapshot metadata
{"epoch": 202604, "tags": ["region:eu-west", "tier:standard"], "applied_at": "2026-03-23T18:12:01Z"}
# runtime behavior
- if request.X-Decision-Epoch == null: attach current local epoch
- if epoch mismatches: if policy.fallback == "allow" -> route using compatible fallback model variant, increment epoch_mismatch_count
  else if policy.fallback == "strict" -> enqueue short wait (<=10ms) for same-epoch route, else fall back
```
kevin_r: nice. I'd prefer to keep the wait bounded and observable. Also need to consider prefetching: when new epoch arrives, proactively push small delta to decision cache in-ram to reduce pull lag.
sam: prefetch + epoch header + canary strict sounds good. But we should also think about probe generation. Right now probes are independent and can amplify the mismatch. Maybe tag probes with origin-epoch and suppress hedges for probes older than a threshold.
anya: yep — probe TTL idea: drop probe-triggered hedges if probe.epoch < local_epoch - 1. That avoids noisy amplification.
maria: test plan: 1) offline sim with mixed-epoch traffic (use sim harness) measuring hedges and p99; 2) staging rollout: epoch-header attach + probe-ttl suppression for 24h; 3) canary: 1% tenants strict mode -> observe routing. We'll need dashboard widgets.
tj: migration notes: policy hot-reload infra must write snapshots atomically and emit a push-notification to router pool; add a small publish/ack handshake so old and new can detect sync. Implementation: policy-service publishes SNS-like message: "snapshot:202604" -> routers receive and ack -> policy-service marks epoch active. Use a fallback window to avoid blocking.
kevin_r: implementation caution: ack fanout can take time regionally. Keep it opportunistic; don't block snapshot activation on 100% ack. Use quorum (e.g., 75%) for strict mode.
sam: deploy-bot: "deploy started" -> deploy-bot: "policy-service v2 deployed to prod at 2026-03-23T18:15:00Z" :rocket:
maria: after deploy, please run sim job id=policy-sim-452 to validate. Also add regression alert if routing.hedge_rate increases >1% from baseline.
anya: one more ask: add an explainability field to responses with decision_epoch and decision_id to make tracing easier for customers (and for postmortem). small response-size tradeoff but huge ops win.
tj: agree. Also add eval harness tests where we re-run critical prompt sets across epoch transitions to catch semantic regressions.
kevin_r: summary action items:
- policy-service: emit epoch pubsub + atomic snapshot write (sam, kevin)
- router runtime: attach/consume X-Decision-Epoch header, bounded wait + fallback policy (anya)
- probes: implement probe-ttl suppression (anya)
- telemetry: routing.epoch_* metrics + Console dashboards (maria)
- rollout: offline sim, staging rollout, 1% canary strict, then ramp (tj)
I'll put a brief RFC followup with diagrams and sim results ETA EOD tomorrow.
sam: thanks all. if anyone wants to pair on the sim config ping me. :thumbsup:
